statuses.label: Qualified or judged
statuses.description: Numerically qualified (a registered protocol passed) or judged (used in a registered experiment), in its declared scope.

statuses.label: Implemented and guarded
statuses.description: On main with its tests and guards: the plan's 'implemented' and 'guarded' levels. Not yet qualified by a registered protocol.

statuses.label: Established
statuses.description: Built earlier and in routine use: older model families and shared infrastructure. Scope and evidence are in each guide.

statuses.label: Designed
statuses.description: A design or protocol is written or accepted; the code is not on main.

statuses.label: Planned
statuses.description: Named in the plan or roadmap, or decided by the user; not started.

statuses.label: Failed qualification
statuses.description: Built, then failed its registered qualification. Kept as evidence and not relied on.

statuses.label: External reference
statuses.description: Outside the engine: a reference simulator or data set, run out of process and compared through saved outputs.

representations.label: Simulated
representations.description: The engine evolves this state step by step, with material, charge and energy accounted for.

representations.label: Modelled in aggregate
representations.description: Represented as a population, count or rate law, not as individual molecules. Shapes drawn for it are illustrations.

representations.label: Prescribed
representations.description: Happens on a schedule the experiment sets; the cell does not decide it.

representations.label: Illustration only
representations.description: Drawn for orientation. Nothing in the engine stands behind it yet.

model_groups.label: Composite tissue model
model_groups.description: resolved_pump_composite@1: the pump tissue model's own step plus declared operators. These parts run together in one model today. Its inner tissue model was rebuilt in place as one modular model, which landed on main on 16 November 2026.

model_groups.label: Earlier tissue families
model_groups.description: The older resolved-tissue families, one module per feature combination. Calcium, fuel, mitochondria, regulation and repair run together here. Their physics moves into the composite model in stages, as uses need it (D167).

model_groups.label: Separate engines
model_groups.description: Models that run on their own: vertex mechanics and the regulatory circuits.

relation_kinds.label: uses
relation_kinds.description: The first part imports the second in the source code.

relation_kinds.label: is an operator of
relation_kinds.description: Registered as an operator of the composite model.

relation_kinds.label: requires
relation_kinds.description: The operator declares that this law must come before it.

relation_kinds.label: writes
relation_kinds.description: The operator declares that it changes this state and books the change.

relation_kinds.label: provides
relation_kinds.description: The operator provides this state to the rest of the model as its current value.

relation_kinds.label: reads
relation_kinds.description: The operator reads a value another operator provides.

relation_kinds.label: cannot combine with
relation_kinds.description: The composite refuses this pair: one operator reads a value as declared while the other changes it, or both provide the same value.

relation_kinds.label: wraps
relation_kinds.description: The composite runs this model's own step.

relation_kinds.label: runs
relation_kinds.description: The experiment runs this engine model or operator.

relation_kinds.label: would extend
relation_kinds.description: A planned or designed part, and what it builds on.

relation_kinds.label: delivers
relation_kinds.description: A plan gate, or a round of work, and a part it is meant to deliver.

relation_kinds.label: is implemented by
relation_kinds.description: A capability and the engine parts behind it.

relation_kinds.label: has its law in
relation_kinds.description: The engine law that acts on this unit is in this part of the engine (from the law inventory, checked against the code).

relation_kinds.label: is drawn in the cell view as
relation_kinds.description: The part of the cell view that stands for this unit.

atlases.label: E. coli
atlases.plain: A rod-shaped bacterium of the animal gut with 4,403 proteins in UniProt's reference proteome of strain K-12. The units of the law inventory are machines of animal cells; this is what the same families' signatures find in it.
method: The organism's proteins are the 4,403 reviewed entries of UniProt's reference proteome UP000000625 (release 2026_04), one protein each.
Licences were read before anything was copied; each is stated in sources.

A unit counts as found only where a protein carries the signature of a family that makes the machine itself (the subunit that forms the channel, or the pump's own chain). A protein that carries only the signature of a family that goes with the machine (a regulator, an accessory subunit) is no candidate: the unit's note names it, and it is listed under extra. This reading is the file's own.
Each unit's family was taken from its own human candidates, by the same InterPro signatures that the planarian, Syn3A and M. pneumoniae atlases ask. The build checks that the candidates carry them.
Each signature was looked for among the InterPro entries UniProt gives each of the 4,403 proteins. No unit's own family was found; 1 protein carries the signature of an accessory family alone.
A control for every signature: how many reviewed UniProtKB entries of all bacteria carry it; each unit's note gives what came back.

8 further signatures, of the channels a bacterium could have (potassium, chloride, magnesium, water and membrane-stretch channels), were looked for as well; the 15 proteins that carry them are listed under extra (the potassium channel domain (kch); the large-conductance mechanosensitive channel (MscL) (mscL); the mechanosensitive channel MscS (mscK, mscM, mscS, ybdG, ybiO and ynaI); chloride channels of the ClC family (clcA, clcB and yfeO); aquaporins and their relatives (major intrinsic proteins) (aqpZ and glpF); CorA-type magnesium channels (corA and zntB)), with the cell's P-type ATPases and the catalytic head of its ATP synthase.
No similarity search was run, and nothing is called an ortholog.
The inventory has 49 units. One of them, an engineered protein cage, is left out of the picture for now: it is a designed protein, not a part of a cell. The 48 others are shown and counted here.

atlases.label: Fruit fly
atlases.plain: The fruit fly of the laboratory, with 13,814 genes in UniProt's reference proteome. This is what the family signatures of Cells' machines find among the one protein shown for each gene.
method: The fly's proteins are the 13,814 of UniProt's gene-by-gene set of the reference proteome UP000000803 (release 2026_04): one for each gene, 3,850 with a reviewed entry and 9,964 with an unreviewed one.
Licences were read before anything was copied; each is stated in sources.
Each unit's family was taken from its own human candidates, by the same InterPro signatures that the other species' atlases ask. The build checks that the candidates carry them.

Each signature was looked for among the InterPro entries UniProt gives each protein. A unit counts as found only where a protein carries the signature of a family that makes the machine itself; an accessory family alone does not make it found.
Where no protein carries the family the engine's law names and proteins carry another family asked for the same machine (innexins, for gap junctions), the finding is 'different family'.

Each product says, apart, how it was found and what its entry is. Found: by the signature of a family that makes the machine itself, which makes it a candidate by family, or only by that of a family that goes with the machine (a regulator, or a subunit that makes no channel or pump by itself), which makes it no candidate for the machine's own work. Its entry: reviewed by a curator, or annotated automatically; that says how the entry was written, not that the protein does the unit's work.
Several units of one family (the Kv1 channels) list the same proteins, and nothing here says which protein does which unit's work.
No similarity search was run, and nothing is called an ortholog.
The inventory has 49 units. One of them, an engineered protein cage, is left out of the picture for now: it is a designed protein, not a part of a cell. The 48 others are shown and counted here.

atlases.label: Planarian
atlases.plain: A freshwater flatworm that regrows its whole body from a fragment; it is the planarian the databases know best, with 1,588 UniProtKB entries, more than all other planarians together, and a chromosome-scale genome with predicted genes.
method: Species: UniProt holds 1,588 entries for Schmidtea mediterranea (4 reviewed), more than half of the 2,784 it holds for all planarians (the order Tricladida; among the others, Dugesia japonica 499, Girardia tigrina 81, Schmidtea polychroa 74, Dugesia ryukyuensis 23), and a proteome for no planarian. WormBase ParaSite holds a chromosome-scale genome assembly of Schmidtea mediterranea with gene models; the assembly is described by Ivanković and others 2024. So the atlas is of Schmidtea mediterranea.
Licences were read before anything was copied; each is stated in sources, and what was read but not copied is in not_copied.

Each unit's family was taken from its own human candidates: the InterPro signatures they carry were read from UniProt, and one or two that mark the family were chosen. The build checks that the candidates carry them.
Curated entries first: UniProt has 4 reviewed entries for the species, and none belongs to a family the atlas draws.
Named in a publication: a planarian protein counts as named only where the saved abstract, or the saved open-access text, of the paper uses the name. 4 products rest on this.

Family signature: unreviewed UniProtKB entries of the species that carry the signature, and gene models that carry it. The gene models are those of one genome annotation (WBPS19 of WormBase ParaSite, assembly schMedS3_haplotype1): 17,294 genes with a predicted protein. The ones the atlas names are listed in data/proteins/planarian/reference_proteins.tsv. A model carries a signature if that annotation's own InterPro matches say so, or if its predicted protein is, letter for letter, a sequence that carries it in UniProt's archive (InterPro 111.0).
A UniProtKB sequence and a gene model are given as one product when at least 80% of the sequence's 8-residue words occur in the model's predicted protein and no other gene reaches half of that share.

Where a signature found nothing, it was also asked of all 98,660 planarian sequences in UniProt's archive, of the UniProtKB entries of all flatworms and of reviewed human entries; the unit's note gives what came back.

Each product says, apart, how it was found (named in a publication, by the signature of a family that makes the machine, or only by that of a family that goes with it, such as a beta subunit or a regulator) and what its record is (a UniProtKB entry, reviewed or not, or a gene model of the genome annotation).

A product found by the signature of a family that makes the machine is a candidate, never an established counterpart; one found only by that of a family that goes with the machine is no candidate for the machine's own work. Counts are gene models in one haplotype of one genome assembly, not genes confirmed in the animal, and short models may be fragments.
No similarity search against other species was run, and no product is called an ortholog.
The inventory has 49 units. One of them, an engineered protein cage, is left out of the picture for now: it is a designed protein, not a part of a cell. The 48 others are shown and counted here.

atlases.label: Thale cress
atlases.plain: A small flowering plant of the laboratory, with 27,368 genes in UniProt's reference proteome. The units of the law inventory are machines of animal cells; this is what their family signatures find among the one protein shown for each gene.
method: The plant's proteins are the 27,368 of UniProt's gene-by-gene set of the reference proteome UP000006548 (release 2026_04): one for each gene, 16,212 with a reviewed entry and 11,156 with an unreviewed one.
Licences were read before anything was copied; each is stated in sources.
Each unit's family was taken from its own human candidates, by the same InterPro signatures that the other species' atlases ask. The build checks that the candidates carry them.

Each signature was looked for among the InterPro entries UniProt gives each protein. A unit counts as found only where a protein carries the signature of a family that makes the machine itself; an accessory family alone does not make it found.

A plant has channels and pumps of families of its own, which no unit of the inventory stands for. They are not listed here: the search asks only for the families of Cells' units. 'Different family' is given only where the inventory's table names another family for the same machine, and it names none that a plant has.

Each product says, apart, how it was found and what its entry is. Found: by the signature of a family that makes the machine itself, which makes it a candidate by family, or only by that of a family that goes with the machine (a regulator, or a subunit that makes no channel or pump by itself), which makes it no candidate for the machine's own work. Its entry: reviewed by a curator, or annotated automatically; that says how the entry was written, not that the protein does the unit's work.
Nothing here says which protein does which unit's work.
No similarity search was run, and nothing is called an ortholog.
The inventory has 49 units. One of them, an engineered protein cage, is left out of the picture for now: it is a designed protein, not a part of a cell. The 48 others are shown and counted here.

cap.membrane.note: It has two membranes. By UniProt's vocabulary the inner one separates the cytoplasm from the periplasm, and the outer one the periplasm from the cell's surroundings. No source read for this file measured a voltage across either.

cap.channels.note: Not the channels of animal cells: none of its proteins carries the signature of a channel family that Cells has a law for. 15 of its proteins carry the signature of a bacterial channel family: the potassium channel domain (kch); the large-conductance mechanosensitive channel (MscL) (mscL); the mechanosensitive channel MscS (mscK, mscM, mscS, ybdG, ybiO and ynaI); chloride channels of the ClC family (clcA, clcB and yfeO); aquaporins and their relatives (major intrinsic proteins) (aqpZ and glpF); CorA-type magnesium channels (corA and zntB).

cap.pumps.note: Not the pumps of animal cells: none of its proteins carries the signature of the sodium-potassium pump. Its P-type ATPases (copA, kdpB, mgtA and zntA) and its ATP synthase are stated to be in the inner membrane.

cap.junctions.why: It lives as single cells and has no gap junctions: none of its proteins carries the signature of connexins or innexins.

cap.extracellular.note: Two spaces lie beyond its inner membrane: the periplasm, between its two membranes, and what surrounds the cell, the lower gut of an animal or wherever it is released.

cap.water.note: By UniProt's vocabulary a wall lies between its two membranes and plays a part in the cell's shape and stability. One of its proteins, AqpZ, carries the signature of the aquaporin family.

cap.calcium.why: It has no endoplasmic reticulum, the store this capability concerns: no entry of its proteome states a place in one, and none of its proteins carries the signature of the store's calcium pump or of its release channels.

cap.energy.note: It lives by respiration and by fermentation, with or without oxygen; its ATP synthase is stated to be in the inner membrane.

cap.mitochondria.why: It is a bacterium and has no mitochondria: no entry of its proteome states a place in one. Its ATP synthase is in the inner membrane.

cap.circuits.note: At the chromosome, which lies in a region of the cytoplasm that no membrane surrounds: there is no nucleus. 64 of its proteins carry UniProt's keyword for two-component regulatory systems.

cap.grn.why: It forms no tissue, so there is nothing for gene networks to be coupled across. Gene expression within the one cell belongs with regulatory circuits.

cap.trafficking.why: It has no endoplasmic reticulum and no Golgi: no entry of its proteome states a place in either. By the names of their entries, its proteins cross or enter the inner membrane through the Sec and Tat translocases.

cap.machines.note: Its ribosomes, RNA polymerase, the ATP synthase, the protein translocases and the motor of its flagella. One of its proteins carries the signature of the proteasome's subunits: its entry names it "ATP-dependent protease subunit HslV".

cap.secretion.note: Some of its proteins are stated to be secreted, and porins and transporters carry molecules across its two membranes. Signalling between its own cells was not looked for.

cap.repair.note: The place would be its envelope. No source read for this file describes an injury of it or its resealing in this organism.

cap.division.note: It divides as a single cell: its proteome names the cell division protein FtsZ.

cap.replacement.why: It forms no tissue, so there is no neighbour for a new cell to replace.

cap.mechanics.why: It forms no sheet: its cells share no edges to pull on. Its own movement, swimming with flagella, is not what this capability models.

cap.sheet.why: It lives as single cells and forms no sheet of coupled cells.

models.label: GARD assembly
models.plain: A model of how heredity could begin before genes: a small assembly of molecules of many types, in which the molecules inside speed the joining and leaving of others, so that a mix of types can grow, split in two and pass something of itself on. It is a model, not an organism: it has no cell, no shape, no place and no clock of real life. The preprint Plastic Heredity uses it.

modelled.text: Designed, not modelled. Its design note is on main, decided on 16 November 2026 (D192); its build started on 17 November, and nothing of GARD is in the engine on main yet. By D197 it is one law set, kept only for comparison with Cells' own origin-of-life engine, whose design is proposed.

levels.shows: Generations across fissions: the line of daughters that carry on, and at each fission how alike the parent and that daughter are. The line at 0.9 is drawn on that comparison only.

clock.says: Its runs count fissions, not seconds: GARD has no clock of real life.

facts.value: 80 molecules, then splits in two

facts.label: In the preprint, a fission is inherited when
facts.value: the similarity H between the parent just before the fission and the daughter that carries on is above 0.9; 0.9 itself is a break

preprint.text: Plastic heredity: Predicting and steering how inheritance breaks, returns, and persists. Preprint, version 5.0. Read for the viewer's note docs/ORIGIN_OF_LIFE.md, whose section 1.1 gives these values from its common experimental framework and its appendix F.

notes.label: The law's two forms, in the engine's design (D192)
notes.text: As D192 records the checked finding: in a closed two-type world, the preprint's single-event kernel generically fails Kolmogorov's cycle criterion (a rank-one catalysis matrix is the exception); the original authors' kernel is not established either way; the preprint's vector-Poisson contracts were not tested; the preprint's driven runs are not affected; the pair-consistent form is exactly reversible. The engine builds both forms, and its first experiment measures the difference. The viewer shows no comparison of the two.

notes.label: Cells' own origin-of-life engine (D197)
notes.text: D197 records the user's words of 17 November 2026: “and we will also do our own first principle engine, GARD is only for comparison”. GARD becomes one declared law set on general machinery: exact stochastic events, assemblies exchanging with a held phase, fission and lineage, a thermodynamic ledger and the run records. Cells' own engine takes its laws from physical chemistry: catalysis that is thermodynamically consistent, physical assemblies, and explicit sources of free energy. Its design note is proposed, with options for the user; nothing of it is built.

entities.label: External modules
entities.plain: Packages maintained outside Cells could add laws and mechanisms that meet the same checks, accounting and execution contracts as the engine's own. Cells stays under the MIT licence, aiming at broad use (the user's direction, D180, 15 November 2026). Each part would be registered explicitly for one model build, then checked, assembled, compiled and run; registering a module that a model does not use changes nothing. The design note is still marked proposed. On 16 November 2026 the user, asking that others can easily add modules and laws by pull request, confirmed its five open decisions (D185). Contributed modules come first inside Cells, each in its own folder and namespace, under the MIT licence and with a named owner. A conformance kit shipped in Cells checks a module before its pull request; passing it means the kit's checks passed, not that the science is qualified. New physics still goes into the engine's source, as modules of its structure. The example module lives in this repository and is the template contributors copy. Development runs record an outside module's identity, and registered and judged runs also freeze its files. Two additions: the engine will write a declarations manifest, a list of every registered law, operator and kind with what it reads, writes and conserves, so that new modules appear in the documents and in this viewer's laws library without hand edits; and a contributor guide with a pull-request template. The four openings the design asked of the rework landed with it on 16 November 2026: kinds of piece are registered for one model build, exactly as an outside package would register them. Laws and operators are still closed tables inside Cells. Its first stage, one law from a separately installed package, is fifth in the plan's order after the landing, with the manifest and the guide. None of it is built yet: the kit, the example module, the manifest and the guide come with that stage. Still open: whether the project lists the modules that pass, and automatic checks on GitHub for outside pull requests.

entities.label: Source layout by role
entities.plain: The user decided on 16 November 2026 (D188) that the engine's source takes the modular layout: each law a module of its own, grouped by mechanism (channels, junctions, pumps, routes, reactions, transport), and folders of their own for kinds, operators, models, numerics, execution, the registry, definitions and records. The older model families move into a folder of legacy code that nothing outside it imports. It is reached by two scripted moves, the older families first, each checked at every commit: the same collected tests, the compiled programs unchanged, all 113 saved worlds the same, and tiers 1 and 2 with no changed outcome. Its first step is done: a read-only tool lists the families from the import graph, and on 16 November 2026 the user settled the list (D189). Nine families stay active, among them four that registered protocols name, whose shared code moves into the modular core; 102 become legacy. Its design note, proposed, and the two scripts that plan, make and check the moves have been on main since 17 November 2026. The note's probe ran the whole cycle on a scratch copy of the tree, never merged: a family moved, a coupled kernel taken out and moved, and every check came out identical. Five refactors came first, on 17 November 2026: the legacy entry point (R1), computed module paths named in full (R2), the parts of seven older modules that active code reaches taken verbatim into the core (R3), and two roots taken from the package instead of from a file's depth (R4, R5). The first move then landed on main the same day: the older families' 334 modules went into src/cells/legacy/ by its committed map, with no hand edits, keeping their sub-packages and their names, with no law, kind, operator or model identifier changed, and every gate held, a continuity resume across the move among them. Move 2, which puts the modular parts into the folders by role, is next; it waits for the user's answer on whether a checkpoint must cross it. The moves are the first step of the order the user set (D194). Files are moved, not rewritten: putting each law's declaration, mathematics and citation in one module is a separate pass. Planned: the first move is made, and the second is not.

entities.label: Packed GPU execution
entities.plain: Many worlds of one structure packed into one batch on the GPU, to keep it busy. On the L4, one world of the 825-node tissue keeps about a quarter of the GPU's processors active; 128 worlds or more keep about 90% active. The same planner is meant to serve production ensembles. Its design was proposed on 15 November 2026, at the user's request, and a planner is built on a branch of its own. In a development run on the L4 on 16 November 2026, packed repeats were identical bit for bit, but packing alone moved some small flux and ledger values by up to 1.6e-8 relative, more than the criterion set for it. The same day this was traced to rounding amplified by the conditioning of the field solve: the moved values are small differences of potentials. The direction ruled judges each field at 1e-12 of the scale it is computed from, with an empirical cap for the outside network's ledgers and an exact check of what the host computes from the state; it is not frozen until a held-out pass on the merged code. The four seams it asked of the core landed with the windows lane on the evening of 16 November 2026: arguments built for each window, a world named on every refusal, a typed refusal for memory, and an opt-in mode that sets a refused world aside and carries on with the others. The planner merges after its own gate, and its one-time GPU qualification runs on the merged code. Not on main.

entities.label: Human cardiac laws
entities.plain: The laws of a human heart muscle cell from the ventricle, so that the engine can run a paced human cell. The user brought them forward on 16 November 2026 (D183), as a lane of their own on the rebuilt tissue model. Their design note, on main since the same day and still proposed, sets out eight new channel laws, two new transporter cycles (the sodium–calcium exchanger and the sodium–potassium pump), a calcium release law, a rapid calcium buffer and a calcium-dependent enzyme, CaMKII, with calcium handling moved into the tissue model in pools that share the cell's potential. Each law is named by its mechanism, not by a protein. The choices were made the same day (D184): the equations and parameters of O'Hara and Rudy's 2011 model of the endocardial cell; that cell type first, and others later as sets of parameters; Hodgkin–Huxley gates for the sodium current; and 310 K. Each law would be checked under voltage clamp against an independent reference. The user approved a whole-cell comparison over one beat for that model only: against an independent reference written from the paper, judged, and against the published model, run unmodified and outside the engine, keeping only its saved outputs, reported and not judged. No engine code is written yet. They are built in step 3 of the order the user set on 16 November 2026 (D194), after D188's moves and one pass over the core's shared seams, in parallel with operator composition and finite fuel. The human living-cell loop waits for these laws.

entities.label: Kind interface
entities.plain: How a new kind of piece joins the tissue model. A kind is one module's contribution: its own fields, and hooks that the tissue model calls at fixed points of its step. Each kind registers itself on a registry that belongs to one model build, exactly as a package from outside Cells would, and a kind that a world does not declare changes nothing. Its name carries a namespace, so an outside kind cannot collide with a built-in one, and the order in which kinds add their fields is fixed by their sorted names. On main since the rework landed on 16 November 2026, with three built-in kinds: passive routes, a rapid proton buffer and transporters. Since the evening of the same day there are two more, for feature request FR-5: the damage of a membrane patch and a pH condition, which act on routes only through the routing door. A test on main registers a planted kind from outside the engine's source and runs it through every seam, and two kinds whose reads of one row could disagree are refused when a world is built. On the evening of 16 November 2026, with the core's next lane, it gained controls that change on a schedule, a routing door through which one kind's factors scale another's routes, and the terms finite fuel needs in the energy accounts. Implemented and guarded.

entities.plain: Each kind of molecule is to have one identity and one conserved total, declared once where a world is defined, however many arrays hold it: free and bound molecules of one kind are one species. Measured on the L4, this costs no measurable time at 16 species, and its sums come out bit for bit the same on the GPU and the CPU. entities.label: Fuel as shared species
entities.plain: Decided on 15 November 2026 (D176): ATP, ADP and phosphate become ordinary species of the shared inventory. Reactions make and spend them, pumps draw from the same amounts, and the standard chemical potential of each is declared in one place. In the design, finite fuel is a transporter's default, and fuel held constant is the special case: a held row of that inventory, not a parameter of a pump. Since the rework landed on 16 November 2026, the species registry holds those standard potentials, and the transporters on main read their fuel as held rows of the inventory; finite fuel is refused there until a later step. The terms finite fuel needs in the kind interface's energy accounts landed the same evening, with the core's next lane; the transporter's own change is still to come. The first case is small: one regeneration reaction and one pump share a finite amount of fuel, and show depletion, a slower pump and recovery. Its independent reference landed on main on 15 November 2026: with regeneration stopped for 200 s, ATP falls almost to nothing and the pump to about 0.2% of its rate; two seconds after regeneration resumes the pump is back within 1%, and every account closes. Its design on the kind interface is accepted, ruled by the lead on 16 November 2026: the transporter gains a second kind of fuel that it moves, one ATP to ADP and phosphate per cycle, so fuel can run down and recover; the first world is the reference's pump of an uncharged molecule, with its store a compartment the cell owns, and the proton pump on finite fuel follows later. The engine's own case, checked against the reference, is built in step 3 of the order the user set on 16 November 2026 (D194), after one pass over the core's shared seams. Where this meets explicit proton chemistry, the boundary is declared for fuel held constant: the fuel's free energy is taken at its node's reference pH, and a stage whose pH strays beyond a declared band is refused. For finite fuel at a node whose protons change it is still open, and refused. That work booked by a reaction is not fuel is still to be declared. Finite fuel runs today only in the earlier tissue families, and the tissue model's own pumps hold their fuel constant. Designed; not on main.

entities.label: Passive permeation law
entities.plain: A law for molecules that cross a membrane on their own, down their gradient: the one law added in the rework round, to show that adding a law changes nothing for worlds that do not use it. Since the rework landed on 16 November 2026 it is on main as one of the tissue model's passive routes, beside a proton leak that compartment pH uses. For an uncharged molecule its core computation is the membrane transport's own route at zero charge, and it books the heat it releases exactly, as the free energy lost by what it moved. In a closed test with two compartments it must conserve material, stop when both sides are at equal chemical potential, reverse with the driving force, and turn the free energy lost into heat with no work from outside. Its independent reference, written by a separate agent that read no engine code, landed on 15 November 2026: in it, flow and heat are exactly zero at equal concentrations, the flow reverses exactly, and heat never decreases. The engine's operator for secretion and uptake is a driven route that books work, so it does not count as passive. Implemented and guarded: on a closed pair of compartments, a test on main shows it relaxing as the independent closed form says, conserving material, and booking as heat the engine's own decrease of free energy, to rounding. It is not numerically qualified, and its composition with water is still a target. Until a later step, the composite model refuses an operator that writes a row such a route books exactly. The minimal-cell track's vesicle tests are its first user.

entities.label: Catalytic assemblies (GARD)
entities.plain: The engine's first model family for the origin of life: assemblies that hold counts of many kinds of molecule, exchange them with a held reservoir, catalyse one another's joining and leaving through a fixed matrix, grow, split at random, and leave lineages, after the GARD model. The design was decided on 16 November 2026 (D192). Events are simulated exactly, one molecule at a time. Assemblies are abstract at first. The catalysis matrix is per-world data with about 100 kinds of molecule. Catalysis comes in two forms: the single-event form of a preprint's reconstruction of GARD, for the comparison, and a pair-consistent form, in which every transfer and its reverse see the same catalysts, as the engine's law. An independent check found that in a closed world of two kinds of molecule the preprint's single-event form generically fails a test of reversibility (a catalysis matrix of rank one is the exception), and that the pair-consistent form is exactly reversible. The original authors' own event rates are not established either way, and the preprint's driven runs are not affected (D192). The first experiment measures the difference between the two forms. The first comparison is with that preprint's reconstruction, three ways, approved by the user: an independent reference, that work's own test code run unchanged outside the engine, and a comparison of distributions on 40 fresh matrices at tolerances set in advance. It is a stochastic family, registered as modules, CPU only, about 20 to 29 agent-days, built in step 4 of the order the user set the same evening (D194). Designed; no engine code.

entities.label: Scoped composition (door S)
entities.plain: How several operators share one field. Before the rework, one operator supplied a field and replaced all of it, so two operators that touch different cells of the same field could not be combined. Since the rework landed on 16 November 2026, an operator can declare which cells or nodes it reads and changes, whether its change adds, multiplies or replaces, and at which stage of the step; the composite model then merges the changes place by place. Two operators that change separate places must give the same result in either order, and an overlap is refused unless a rule says how to combine it. Tests on main show its acceptance: two operators on separate places give the same bits in either order, and an overlap is refused unless both changes commute. In the round, operators that close cells still change whole masks, and the one pair newly admitted is the scheduled bath beside the shared-inventory reactions; the other pairs keep their refusals. With it the chain that is its test case runs with every ledger closing: a dose in the bath, taken up into a compartment, reacting there. Implemented and guarded, not numerically qualified.

entities.label: Compartment pH (FR-4)
entities.plain: Protons as a species, a pump that acidifies a compartment against its gradient, and buffering (feature request FR-4), one of the two priority users of the modular rework (D176). Its pump, its buffer and a proton leak landed on main with the rework on 16 November 2026, as pieces of the tissue model, together with the drivers that build its first world and the tools for its qualification. In a development run of that world, which is not a verdict, the compartment's pH stays within 1.4e-12 of the independent reference at a step of 1 ms, the energy accounts converge at second order as the step shrinks, and the planted errors are caught. Its independent references, written by a separate agent that read no engine code, show the compartment acidifying from pH 7.2 to about 5.1 against its gradient while the cytoplasm stays within 0.02 pH; without the counterion route it stalls. A kernel for treating the compartment's membrane implicitly in the step is on main too, with its tests; no model uses it yet, and chloride and pores wait for it. Implemented and guarded; nothing is judged. Its protocol is proposed, and its registration and judged run are the plan's next item.

One holds today: a molecule's amount regulating an electrical response, which is the coupling operator's qualification of 15 November 2026. The other three are targets. A dose in the bath taken up into a compartment and reacting there is door S's own test world: since the rework landed on 16 November 2026 it runs with every ledger closing, guarded and not numerically qualified. A reaction and a pump sharing a finite amount of fuel comes after FR-4 and FR-5 in the plan's order. A neutral molecule with water in a vesicle needs the passive law, which landed with the rework; the law's composition with water does not exist yet. Each joins the results gate as it lands. A new organism or experiment should add engine physics only for a mechanism the engine lacks.

entities.label: Results baseline
entities.plain: The tool behind the rework's results gate. It saves what a defined set of worlds computes at a tagged version, on the CPU, and compares a later version with it, bit for bit or within a declared tolerance; a refused run must be refused in the same way. A second tool lists the engine models that each registered protocol names, so that the protocols a change affects can be run again. Validation code with its own tests in the routine gate, on main since 15 November 2026. On 16 November 2026 the 825-node world's bits at binding were found to depend on the number of processors a run uses, so the comparison now records that number and compares runs only at equal counts; the user decided the same evening to remove the dependence by running the linear algebra on one thread (D190). That pin merged on 17 November 2026, and the baseline's record of its environment now names each library's thread count.

entities.label: Test tiers gate
entities.plain: The routine gate: every test file's outcome is compared with a recorded baseline before code lands. A file counts as changed when its exit code or its count of failures or errors differs, when its count of passing tests falls, or when its count of skipped tests rises. At D172's landing on 16 November 2026, tiers 1 and 2 (492 files) showed no changed outcome. Of tier 3's 229 files, 187 passed, and each of the other 42 was classified, none of them a defect of the round: 23 failures and 16 time-outs that were there before, two tests the round left stale, fixed in the next commit, and one that passes when run alone. The user's rule of the same day (D187) is to test as little as possible but enough for the science: each claim is proved once, at the cheapest level that can prove it, a new test must catch a planted error, and each landing's tier-3 table is frozen as the record the next run is compared with. The audit's tools merged on the evening of 16 November 2026: tier 3's table is frozen test by test, so that a later run of tier 3 is compared test by test instead of running old code again. The user approved the audit's firm list of tests to retire the same evening (D189), and the retire merged early on 17 November 2026: 11 whole files of tier 3 and 40 of tiers 1 and 2 were deleted, and 811 cases were removed from 42 more, while eight rows were held instead, each with its reason. The tiers now hold 327, 152 and 222 files, and tier 3's frozen record holds 218 files and 6,869 tests. The saving is 5.5 processor-hours per run of tier 3 and 2 minutes per gate of tiers 1 and 2. The tree before the retire is tagged, so that every retired test stays recoverable.

entities.label: Results gate
entities.plain: How the rework was accepted, and, through its comparison of saved worlds, how changes built on it are checked. A machine-readable list names every scientific result that must still hold, and the gate fails if any of them did not actually run. Every saved world is run before and after on the CPU and compared field by field (G1). At the landing, every registered protocol that uses the tissue model was also run again and had to keep its verdict (G2); the user held E07-v1's re-run, whose worlds the comparison covers instead (D181). The rework landed through it on 16 November 2026: all 113 saved worlds were the same bit for bit before the round's last change, and within its declared tolerance after it, and every registered small protocol run again passed. The comparison of saved worlds is what is in use since: it ran again at the core's next lane, at the core's fixes and on main a83d8f15, all 113 worlds the same bit for bit each time. The protocols' re-run (G2) ran at the landing and is not repeated for each lane: a lane whose comparison of saved worlds is bit for bit moves no registered result. Two parts are still owed, each shown as a part of its own: the planted changes that it must catch (G3), and the measurements of compile time, memory and run time (G4). Both run once with tier 3 of the tests on the source tree as D188's moves leave it (D194). The comparison's own planted-difference self-test is a test on main, and the routine test gate also flags a test file whose count of passing tests falls or whose count of skipped tests rises.

syn3a.note: None of the 455 protein products of its genome carries the signature of BK calcium-activated potassium channels, SK calcium-activated potassium channels and BK channel beta subunits (IPR047871, IPR015449, IPR003930). UniProtKB holds 4 entries of other mollicutes, the class of bacteria it was made from, that carry one of them. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. It takes up potassium with a transporter instead (KtrAB, listed under extra). No ion channel of any family searched was found in this organism: its ions cross the membrane through transporters and pumps.

mpneumoniae.note: None of the 688 protein products of its genome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it belongs to, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

planarian.note: By their signatures, planarians have innexins and no connexins. 68 planarian gene models carry the innexin signature and none the connexin one; no UniProtKB entry of any flatworm carries the connexin signature either, while 21 reviewed human entries do. One planarian innexin has a sequence record of its own, smedinx-11. More is to be read in Abascal and Zardoya 2013, on which animals have each family, and in Oviedo and Levin 2007, on that innexin; neither states an open licence, so nothing is taken from them. Which innexins a general gap-junction law would stand for is not known.

syn3a.note: None of the 455 protein products of its genome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it was made from, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

thalecress.note: None of its 27,368 proteins carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. A plant's cells are joined in another way: by plasmodesmata, channels lined by the cell membrane that cross the wall between two cells (UniProt's vocabulary). 32 proteins of the catalogue are stated to be there; they stand on the cell membrane's shelf.

entities.label: Cx45/Cx45 homotypic gap-junction channel
entities.plain: A channel that joins two neighbouring cells, so ions and small molecules pass straight from one to the other. Each cell contributes a ring of six connexins.
entities.note: Only in the nominal compatibility profile of emt_mirna_pair@1.

mpneumoniae.note: None of the 688 protein products of its genome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it belongs to, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

planarian.note: There is no connexin 45 to find in a planarian: by its signatures it has innexins, another family of gap-junction proteins, and no connexins. 68 planarian gene models carry the innexin signature and none the connexin one; no UniProtKB entry of any flatworm carries the connexin signature either, while 21 reviewed human entries do. One planarian innexin has a sequence record of its own, smedinx-11. More is to be read in Abascal and Zardoya 2013, on which animals have each family, and in Oviedo and Levin 2007, on that innexin; neither states an open licence, so nothing is taken from them. Nothing says which innexins, if any, would form a channel like this one.

lines: 437 amino acids

syn3a.note: None of the 455 protein products of its genome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it was made from, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

thalecress.note: None of its 27,368 proteins carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. A plant's cells are joined in another way: by plasmodesmata, channels lined by the cell membrane that cross the wall between two cells (UniProt's vocabulary). 32 proteins of the catalogue are stated to be there; they stand on the cell membrane's shelf.

entities.label: Cx40/Cx37 heterotypic gap-junction channel
entities.plain: A channel that joins two neighbouring cells, so ions and small molecules pass straight from one to the other. Each cell contributes a ring of six connexins.

mpneumoniae.note: None of the 688 protein products of its genome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it belongs to, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

planarian.note: There is no connexin 40 or connexin 37 to find in a planarian: by its signatures it has innexins, another family of gap-junction proteins, and no connexins. 68 planarian gene models carry the innexin signature and none the connexin one; no UniProtKB entry of any flatworm carries the connexin signature either, while 21 reviewed human entries do. One planarian innexin has a sequence record of its own, smedinx-11. More is to be read in Abascal and Zardoya 2013, on which animals have each family, and in Oviedo and Levin 2007, on that innexin; neither states an open licence, so nothing is taken from them. Nothing says which innexins, if any, would form a channel like this one.

syn3a.note: None of the 455 protein products of its genome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it was made from, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

thalecress.note: None of its 27,368 proteins carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. A plant's cells are joined in another way: by plasmodesmata, channels lined by the cell membrane that cross the wall between two cells (UniProt's vocabulary). 32 proteins of the catalogue are stated to be there; they stand on the cell membrane's shelf.
